title: Inverse-transpose factorization for open source composition
statement:
Fix a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ and a prime $\ell\ne p$. All schemes are separated of finite type over $k$, and all maps are $k$-morphisms [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a unital homomorphism of finite commutative rings killed by powers of $\ell$, and choose $N=\ell^n\geq1$ annihilating both. On either the ordinary etale or pro-etale site let $\mathcal C_{T,R}=D^b_{ctf}(T,R)$ mean the full category of constant-$R$ module complexes with bounded constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude: tensor with any degree-zero module sheaf has cohomology in one fixed finite interval [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf, def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude, det-sp-et-proet-adjunction-transfer]. Write $T_T=-\otimes^L_{A_T}B_T$ [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor, lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings].
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ a quasi-compact open immersion; put $g=fj$ [def-weil-open-immersion]. Choose compactifications with separated finite-type middle schemes [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. On the pro-etale finite-Tor categories let $F_{h,R}=Rh_{!,R}\dashv G_{h,R}=h_R^!$ have counit $\epsilon_{h,R}$, for $h=f,g$ and $R=A,B$ [sk-prop-sf-rf-shriek-preservation]. Let $J_R=Dj_{!,R}\dashv U_R=j_R^*$ have its actual open counit $v_R$ [det-sf-mate-open-restriction]. Use the canonical compact-support composition and refinement comparisons to identify $F_{g,R}=F_{f,R}J_R$ and, adjunction-preservingly, $G_{g,R}=U_RG_{f,R}$ [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction, lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility]. Let $b_f:T_YF_{f,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{f,B}T_X$, $b_g:T_YF_{g,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{g,B}T_U$, and $b_j:T_XJ_A\xrightarrow{\sim}J_BT_U$ be the specified proper-counit/open-tensor comparisons [det-sp-reduction-direct-image], with $b_j$ normalized by the identity proper compactification of $j$.
For $K\in\mathcal C_{Y,A}$ put $M=G_{f,A}K$ and $L=U_AM=G_{g,A}K$. Then the following equalities hold for these specified comparisons on arbitrary pro-etale finite-Tor input, including comparisons through any common refinement:
$$\epsilon_{g,R,H}=\epsilon_{f,R,H}\circ F_{f,R}(v_{R,G_{f,R}H})\qquad(H\in\mathcal C_{Y,R}),$$
$$b_g(L)=F_{f,B}(b_j(L))\circ b_f(J_AL),$$
and
$$\begin{aligned}
T_Y(\epsilon_{g,A,K})\circ b_g(L)^{-1}
={}&T_Y(\epsilon_{f,A,K})\circ b_f(M)^{-1}\circ F_{f,B}(T_X(v_{A,M}))\circ F_{f,B}(b_j(L)^{-1}).
\end{aligned}$$
The last equality is between morphisms $F_{g,B}T_UL\to T_YK$. No smoothness of $f$, flatness of $B$ over $A$, or exceptional scalar mate is assumed.

proof.text: Use the stipulated adjunction-preserving identifications with $F_{f,R}J_R\dashv U_RG_{f,R}$. The composite adjunction definition gives its counit at $H$ as $\epsilon_{f,R,H}\circ F_{f,R}(v_{R,G_{f,R}H})$. This proves the first equality for each $R=A,B$ and every $H$; the actual open counit is the inner counit, not an arbitrarily chosen map.

For any $Q\in\mathcal C_{U,A}$, the finite-Tor comparison equivalence supplies $E\in D^b_{ctf}(U_{et},A)$ and an isomorphism $s:\nu_U^*E\xrightarrow{\sim}Q$. Its hypotheses are exactly the standing schemes and the finite rings of this item. The same node ensures that $E_B$ and the etale compact-support images used in composition lie in the required finite-Tor categories. Thus the etale-origin input condition of the coefficient-composition theorem can be met without restricting $Q$.

The definition of the normalized comparison is $b_{i,p}=Rp_{*,B}(e_i)\circ\gamma_p(i_!^A(-))$. For the identity proper compactification of $j$, the proper factor $\gamma_{1_X}$ is identity under the canonical identity-functor identifications: its defining transpose is the scalar extension of the identity counit. Hence the comparison for $j$ in the coefficient-composition theorem is exactly the specified $b_j=e_j$, with its fixed open normalization.

Invert Step 4 at $L$ and use functoriality: $b_g(L)^{-1}=b_f(J_AL)^{-1}\circ F_{f,B}(b_j(L)^{-1})$. Naturality of $b_f$ at $v_{A,M}:J_AL\to M$ reads $F_{f,B}(T_X(v_{A,M}))\circ b_f(J_AL)=b_f(M)\circ T_Y(F_{f,A}(v_{A,M}))$. Multiplying by the two inverses yields $T_Y(F_{f,A}(v_{A,M}))\circ b_f(J_AL)^{-1}=b_f(M)^{-1}\circ F_{f,B}(T_X(v_{A,M}))$. Substitute this and Step 1 into $T_Y(\epsilon_{g,A,K})\circ b_g(L)^{-1}$; associativity gives exactly the last displayed equality. Its successive objects, starting at the right, are $F_{g,B}T_UL$, $F_{f,B}T_XJ_AL$, $F_{f,B}T_XM$, $T_YF_{f,A}M$, and $T_YK$.

For any specified refinement comparison $\phi_R:F_{h,R}^c\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{h,R}^{c\prime}$, the cited refinement equation is $b_h^{c\prime}T_Y(\phi_A)=\phi_BT_Ub_h^c$ on etale-origin inputs. Both sides are natural transformations with source $T_YF_{h,A}^c$. Applying naturality at $s:\nu^*E\simeq Q$ as in Step 4 and cancelling $T_YF_{h,A}^c(s)$ proves the same equation for all finite-Tor inputs. The cited theorem includes every common refinement and coherent composition. Use these coefficient squares in Steps 3--5 and the stipulated counit-preserving adjunction identifications in Step 1; the same substitutions prove the displayed equalities for those comparisons as well.
